summary.text: Limestone is a carbonate sedimentary rock made mostly of calcite and aragonite, two crystal forms of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃.
It forms when these minerals settle out of water holding dissolved calcium, and for the last 540 million years living things such as corals and shells have likely played the larger part.
Because rainwater slowly dissolves it, exposed limestone often wears into karst landscapes, and most cave systems lie in limestone bedrock.

facts.label: Petroleum reservoirs
facts.value: About 30% of the world's sit in limestone

facts.label: Crushing strength
facts.value: Dense limestone reaches up to 180 MPa

items.prompt: Explorers map a region riddled with caves, where rainwater has slowly carved passages through the bedrock. Which rock is that bedrock most likely to be?
items.explain: Limestone dissolves slightly in rainwater, so exposed limestone erodes into karst, and most cave systems are found in it.

items.prompt: A hiker splits a pale block of carbonate rock and finds bits of shell and coral all through it. Why is this so common in this rock?

options.label: Creatures burrowed into it after it hardened
Rivers washed shells into its cracks much later
Shells grow inside it as crystals form
Most of its grains are leftover sea-creature parts

items.explain: Most grains in limestone are skeletal fragments of marine organisms like coral, which leave their calcite or aragonite structures behind when they die.

items.prompt: A limestone layer is packed with coral fragments rather than bryozoan ones. What kind of water did it most likely form in?

options.label: Water too deep for any waves

items.explain: Coral grains are more common in high-energy settings with strong currents and turbulence, while bryozoan grains favour quiet water.

items.prompt: Chalk is a very porous kind of limestone. Compared with the densest limestone, how would a same-sized block of chalk weigh?

options.label: Heavier, since its pores fill with extra calcite
The same, since the mineral is the same
Lighter, since pores take up much of its volume
Heavier, since chalk holds more magnesium

items.explain: Limestone density depends on porosity, which runs from 0.1% in the densest limestone to 40% in chalk, so chalk sits at the light end.

items.prompt: Where did most of the world's limestone form?

options.label: The floors of the deepest oceans

items.explain: Most limestone formed in shallow marine settings such as continental shelves or platforms, with smaller amounts elsewhere.

items.prompt: Much of the carbonate rock called dolomite did not form directly. What did it usually start out as?

options.label: Limestone that was later chemically altered

items.explain: Much dolomite is secondary dolomite, made when limestone is chemically altered.
